author: Mo Qureshi
headline: Jotun, El Seif and Sesco Steel among Saudi Mega Projects partners
deck: The attending partner list runs to coatings, contracting, engineering, law and heavy lifting equipment.
excerpt: The attending partner list at Saudi Mega Projects runs to coatings, contracting, engineering, law and heavy lifting — a map of which trades expect the next award cycle.
content:
Conference speaker lists describe who has something to say. Partner lists describe who is paying to be in the room, and at Saudi Mega Projects in Riyadh that list is a useful read on which parts of the supply chain expect work.

The attending partners include Jotun and Henkel Polybit in coatings and construction chemicals, Nesma and Partners and El Seif in contracting, KEO in engineering and architecture, Pinsent Masons in law, Sesco Steel in structural steel, and Favelle Favco in heavy lifting equipment.

Each of those represents a different position in the award cycle. Contractors like Nesma and Partners and El Seif are bidding for packages now. Structural steel and crane suppliers sell into work that has already been awarded and is mobilising, which makes their presence a bet on volume rather than on winning any particular job. Coatings and construction chemicals sit later still, specified during design but delivered through the build. A law firm attends because contract disputes and claims are a growing feature of programmes running against fixed deadlines.

Favelle Favco's presence is the most specific signal of the group. Tower cranes of the capacity used on giga-project sites are a constrained resource with long lead times, and crane availability is a genuine determinant of programme sequencing. A crane manufacturer attending a delivery conference is there because clients want to know whether lifting capacity will be available when their programme needs it.

Jotun and Henkel Polybit both feature in this publication's existing coverage of the Saudi construction chemicals market, where the pattern has been international manufacturers moving production closer to the projects rather than shipping into them. The same firms appear at the Middle East Coatings Show in Dubai at the end of the month, which is the upstream half of that business.

MEED puts around $130bn of giga-project work already awarded and roughly $200bn currently in the market. Those are the organiser's figures, and the ratio between them is what the partner list is responding to: more work still to be let than has been let so far.

Sesco Steel's position connects to a structural issue this publication has covered at length. Saudi Arabia has been addressing its steel plate gap through the Ras Al-Khair mill, but construction by weight mostly wants long products, and the fabrication capacity that turns steel into structure is a separate constraint from the capacity that makes the steel.

Partner names are taken from the organiser's published material. A partner list is a paid position, which is what separates it from a delegate list as a signal of commercial intent.
